main_body: Snow-covered cabin: a large snow roof slope (rows ~8-50) above a wooden plank front wall (rows 52-76) with arched double door, two lit windows and wreaths
top_band: Snow roof slope, white to pale blue-grey, rows ~8-50 (about 40 rows), ending in a lighter eave edge at rows 47-50. It reads as a large sloped roof surface seen from above, with a front face of wall below.
evidence: In a column through the middle, the snow roof covers rows 8-50 as a wide horizontal-banded slope with a bright front edge at about rows 47-49. Directly under it at row 51-53 is a darker shadow row with icicles, then the plank wall (rows 53-76) with the door, which has dark frame/iron bands, and inset windows with sills and snow caps. Like the Beodeul house references, the roof is a big visible top slope above the front wall. Roof is tall compared with the wall, but it is the roof surface of the building, so it passes the 3/4 contract.

style.evidence: The snow roof uses about 5 tones (white, pale blue, mid blue-grey, deeper blue-grey, shadow) with per-row drift bands, scalloped shadow dots, and mossy patches. The wood wall has several browns with plank grain, and the door has iron bands, handles and an orange threshold. Outlines are dark navy next to snow and dark brown next to wood, so they follow the adjacent material rather than being neutral black. Windows have warm glow in several tones, wreaths are shaded, and icicles add detail. The richness is comparable to the references, with no large flat fills; the lower wall has slightly repetitive plank stripes but still varies in tone.
